context: 強いて挙げるなら、時間が足りなかったことが問題【だった】。
english: If I had to point out something, the problem was that we didn't have enough time.
note: The marked word is the past tense form of the copula だ, which is だった.

context: 難しい試験【だった】が、どうやら合格できたようだ。
english: It was a difficult exam, but it seems I somehow managed to pass.
note: The marked word is the past tense form of the copula だ, which is だった.

context: 自分の意見を他人に強いて【はいけない】。
english: You shouldn't force your opinions on others.
note: The marked word is a grammatical construction, not a single word.

context: It is most often negated: 強いて〜必要はない (there is no need to force it), 強いて【はいけない】 (you must not force it). A plain affirmative sounds stiff and literary.
note: The marked word is a grammatical construction, not a single word.

context: この街には【おしゃれな】カフェがたくさんある。
english: There are many stylish cafes in this town.
note: The marked word is the entry's word plus the 'na' particle.

context: 情けをかけて【くれた】人を忘れない。
english: I won't forget the person who showed me kindness.
note: The marked word is the past tense form 'くれた' of the verb 'くれる'.
This is the adnominal form 'な' of the copula 'だ', used to modify a noun ('仕事'). The entry is for the plain copula 'だ'.

context: 今までの人生を振り返ってみると、あの出会いが一番大きな転機【だった】。
english: Looking back on my life so far, that encounter was the biggest turning point.
note: This is the past tense form 'だった' of the copula 'だ'.
